transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-04
Time: 3:00 PM PT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Malcolm Reed (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood Solutions Eng); Samir Patel (Mariner Head of Search), Ava Chen (Mariner ML Eng), Tom Ward (Mariner Platform)

Auto-summary: Quick hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + reranker flow for Mariner's internal search. Reviewed Console for per-route tracing, Optimize suggestions (batching/caching), and discussed pilot scope (sample dataset benchmarking). Security and residency briefly validated; next step is pilot proposal and benchmark run.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: hey everyone thanks for joining. this is lena from Redwood, im the AE on the account. quick intro, malcolm will walk through the hosted relevance flow and priya will show a couple console screens.
[00:12] Samir Patel: thanks lena, appreciate it. short agenda from our side — we want to see an end-to-end hosted embeddings + rerank flow, understand latency/cost tradeoffs, and what a pilot would look like.
[00:22] Malcolm Reed: great. quick validation — you're currently running a BM25 baseline in-house right? ava, can you confirm what your infra looks like?
[00:28] Ava Chen: yes we have an elasticsearch cluster for the index and a microservice that calls our re-ranker (lightweight NN model). most queries are under 512 tokens but we do have some longer product descriptions for freight quotes. throughput is about 150 QPS at peak, p95 latency requirement is ~250ms.
[00:45] Tom Ward: also important — data residency. we need logs retained for 90 days and audit trails for ops. SOC2 is a must.
[00:52] Lena Ortiz: noted. Redwood hosted meets SOC2 — we'll share the security pack after this call. also hosted has config for data retention and audit logs in the Console.
[01:05] Malcolm Reed: ok jumping into the flow: the pattern we recommend is two-stage — an embeddings-based retrieval over your vector store, then Redwood's rerank endpoint to refine top-K. i'll share a quick diagram in the chat.
[01:20] Ava Chen: when you say rerank endpoint, is that a llama-based model or something lighter?
[01:26] Malcolm Reed: good question — the hosted reranker can be a tuned LLM variant or smaller cross-encoder. you pick the model from the catalog — for Mariner we usually recommend a mid-sized cross-encoder for latency, or a quantized LLM if you need more semantics.
[01:40] Samir Patel: how do you handle KV cache and prefix caching? our use-case has a lot of similar user prompts for tracking references.
[01:47] Malcolm Reed: Redwood's runtime supports KV cache for autoregressive calls and we do prefix-caching for repeated query prefixes. for rerank (cross-encoder) caching is heavier but we can cache embeddings and top-K id lists to avoid re-computing large parts of the pipeline. small note — sometimes transcription says K-V as like key value — the system logs call it k-v cache in traces.
[02:10] [Screen share: Malcolm shows Console]
[02:18] Malcolm Reed: here's the Console routes page — per-route latency, token breakdown, and traces. you can pin a route to use a hosted model version and set a fallback to lower-cost variant. see the trace for this sample request — notice batching windows and the per-token CPU/GPU split.
[02:40] Ava Chen: is batching automatic or manual? we can't change client code easily.
[02:45] Priya Kapoor: auto-batching is on by default in the hosted runtime. we provide suggestions in Optimize for batch window size and the console proposes per-route recommendations. for client-side changes you can optionally use the batching SDK to push multiple requests together but not required.
[03:05] Tom Ward: and what about throughput guarantees? if we go hosted and hit 150 QPS, will we get throttled?
[03:11] Lena Ortiz: hosted has rate limits per plan, and for higher throughput we can recommend a Dedicated reservation. for pilots, most customers run a hosted pilot and we monitor SLOs; if sustained high QPS is needed we talk Dedicated. also automatic fallback policies can route to cheaper models if capacity constrained.
[03:30] Samir Patel: tell us about pricing — token-based? embedding unit too?
[03:33] Lena Ortiz: yes hosted is usage-based. embeddings have a per-vector price and reranker/token is billed per input+output token. we'll include a tailored pricing sheet in the proposal that shows cost per 1M queries with assumptions on top-K size and average tokens.
[03:53] [Screen share: Priya shows Optimize tab]
[03:58] Priya Kapoor: Optimize analyzes your traffic (or sample logs) and suggests quantization and batching settings. here's a sample suggestion — for Mariner's query profile we think int8 quant on the reranker reduces tokens/sec cost by ~30% with minimal quality loss. also suggests caching top-500 frequent queries.
[04:20] Ava Chen: what's the expected p95 advantage vs our current NN re-ranker?
[04:24] Malcolm Reed: depends, but for similar compute budget we see better semantic recall on hard queries and similar latency with quantization + batching. in internal tests p95 latency is often under 200ms for cross-encoders at top-10 rerank if the model is small/quantized and batching is tuned.
[04:45] Tom Ward: curious about data isolation — if we run hosted will our data be accessible by others?
[04:51] Lena Ortiz: hosted is tenant-isolated; logs and model inputs are encrypted and stored per-customer. for stricter isolation we offer Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. we'll outline options in the proposal.
[05:05] [Interruption — background noise]
[05:12] Samir Patel: sorry — quick question on evals. can we tie quality regressions to our test prompts? we have a set of 500 golden queries.
[05:18] Malcolm Reed: yes, Redwood's evals can attach to per-prompt performance and send regressions alerts — you can lock down a prompt set and run model comparisons. the Console shows delta in metrics after a rollout.
[05:30] Ava Chen: for the pilot, how do we run a benchmark? do you require us to push data to Redwood?
[05:36] Priya Kapoor: for hosted pilot we usually ask for sample queries and anonymized documents or a small snapshot. we run the benchmark in a dedicated sandbox with retention controls. alternatively if you cannot share data you can run a local runner using Redwood's quickstart and we provide scripts to replay logs against the hosted models.
[05:58] Samir Patel: what about SSO and RBAC for the Console?
[06:02] Lena Ortiz: we support SAML/SSO, SSO provisioning, and role-based access controls. audit logs are available and you can restrict access to routes. we'll share the security pack that outlines these features.
[06:18] [Malcolm walks through rerank API payload sample]
[06:25] Malcolm Reed: here's the typical flow: 1) call /embeddings endpoint with query to get vector, 2) top-K retrieval from your vector DB, 3) call /rerank endpoint with query + top-K docs as context. the rerank payload supports structured metadata (doc ids, scores) and you can ask for score outputs to re-weight your results.
[06:47] Ava Chen: does rerank accept per-document embeddings to avoid re-embedding?
[06:50] Malcolm Reed: yes you can pass cached embeddings for the docs and only send the query embedding. that reduces token cost and speeds up the pipeline.
[07:02] Tom Ward: any special handling for very long documents? we have freight docs that are multi-k paragraphs.
[07:08] Malcolm Reed: for long docs we recommend chunking and storing chunk-level embeddings with document pointers. the reranker can then assemble context from top chunks. Console can show coverage metrics to tune chunk size.
[07:28] Samir Patel: what's the onboarding timeline? we need a pilot by end of next month ideally.
[07:33] Lena Ortiz: typical pilot is 3-4 weeks: week 1 onboarding + data sample, week 2 benchmark runs, week 3 qualitative evaluation + recommendations. we can compress some steps.
[07:45] Ava Chen: any red flags on integration complexity? our platform is Kubernetes based and we use private VPC peering for external services.
[07:53] Priya Kapoor: hosted calls over TLS; for VPC/private peering we offer Redwood Private or Dedicated with private networking. many customers start hosted pilot and then shift to VPC when ready.
[08:07] Tom Ward: security pack and the SOC2 doc would be great. also we need an estimate for monthly cost at 150 QPS.
[08:13] Lena Ortiz: we'll provide a cost model in the proposal — Malcolm will run some estimates off your top-queries profile.
[08:22] [Wrap-up recap]
[08:24] Lena Ortiz: recap: 1) Mariner will run a hosted pilot focused on embeddings + rerank, 2) Mariner provides sample queries and docs, 3) Redwood will run benchmark and return latency/cost and Optimize recommendations, 4) share SOC2/security pack and tailored pricing.
[08:40] Samir Patel: that sounds good. can we schedule the benchmark for 2026-05-12?
[08:44] Malcolm Reed: yes, we'll tentatively book that and confirm once we have the sample data.
[08:52] Ava Chen: i'll export top queries and a doc sample by 2026-05-08.
[08:56] Lena Ortiz: perfect. thanks everyone — we'll send the proposal and security docs after the call.
[09:05] Tom Ward: thanks, bye.
